question: What does a higher $\alpha$ value imply in the fitted van Genuchten retention curve? (Mark ALL correct answers)
success: ✅ Yes! A higher $\alpha$ shifts the retention curve toward lower suction and is associated with a lower characteristic air-entry suction.
error: ❌ Not quite. $\alpha$ mainly controls the suction scale and horizontal position of the retention curve; it does not determine the residual water content.

question: How do you recognize a good model fit to retention data? (Mark ALL correct answers)
success: ✅ Correct. A good fit reproduces magnitude, shape, and trend; exact data matching is not required.
error: ❌ Fitting isn't about perfection; it’s about representing trends with minimal bias.

question: Which parameter affects the steepness or curvature of the transition zone in the θ–h curve? (Mark ALL correct answers)
success: ✅ Yes. α scales the horizontal axis; n controls the steepness of the transition.
error: ❌ θr and θs define vertical bounds, not curvature.

question: If the model underestimates water content at intermediate suction values, what should you consider adjusting? (Mark ALL correct answers)
success: ✅ Good. Adjusting α and n can improve the shape of the transition zone.
error: ❌ Ks doesn't affect θ–h; and θr only shifts the curve base.
